agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager would see audited signed training records, a documented 20-to-12-hour redesign and a candid GMP gap backed by a course already underway, and that is likely enough to earn a phone screen, although the unstated June 14 start date could hurt the letter later.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the unsupported 'cut training in half' claim and stays with the real facts, but lines like 'no one does the work until their training is complete' and 'ready to keep accurate records from the start' go a little beyond what the brief supports.

works_the_facts.reason: It uses the 20-to-12 hours, 41% to 58% and the two state audits accurately, but it never turns them into stronger true forms such as a 40% cut, 16 trainer-hours saved a year, or a 17-point (41% relative) rise in the pass rate.

right_comparison.reason: Before/after comparisons for the training hours and the pass rate are given as trends, but the letter never sets the candidate against the real alternative, a hire who has GMP experience but lacks proof of having shortened training and passed audits.

qualification.reason: The GMP hedge says only 'finishes in May' instead of May 2, and the letter leaves out the June 14 earliest start, so the reader cannot check timing against the role's needs.

objections.reason: It deals head-on with the main worries: no regulated-industry background, no GMP records experience and an unfamiliar LMS. It misses the practical objections about availability, namely the start date and interview windows.

fit.reason: This is a properly addressed one-page cover letter, but it uses '[Your Name]' placeholders even though the applicant's name was available.
